4.1.3 . Rewards
The rewards obtained by each agent are state dependent. What this means is that each agent minimizes the deviation of its predicted stochastic parameter from the actual value at each state–action pair. Since fundamentally the L-MADRL abstracts the feasibility and technicality checks to the bi-level framework, the reward formulation is divided into two categories;
R _ { 1 }
and
R _ { 2 } ,
where
R _ { 1 }
represents the reward vector comprising the individual rewards obtained by agent 1 to agent n, depending on the problem case being studied. In general,
R _ { 1 }
is given by:
R _ { 1 } = [ r _ { 1 } , \; r _ { 2 } , \; r _ { 3 } , \; \ldots \; , \; r _ { n } ] ^ { T }\tag{95}
Where
r _ { 1 }   =   r _ { 2 }   =   r _ { n }

r _ { 1 } = \beta _ { \mathrm { c o e f } } ( S P - \hat { S P } _ { \mathrm { t r a n s } } )\tag{96}

S P

The second part of the reward formulation,
R _ { 2 } ,
is the penalty value derived from the feasibility checks when the transformed stochastic parameters
\hat { S P } _ { \mathrm { t r a n s } }

Consequently, the total reward obtained is the summation of these two reward categories, however, since by default DRL seeks to maximize rewards, but in this case, the problem formulation seeks to minimize deviations, the total reward is prefixed with a negative sign so it conforms to the DRL framework.
